name: zzV1_bodies3

tests.name: every skin was photographed at deepest night and at noon
at night the BODY is not mostly crushed to black

detail.note: the body is every cell of the figure that is not one of its own lights. This is the reading the founder's 'illuminated subject, not a glowing object in blackness' actually asks for, and raising eye glow cannot move it.

tests.name: and it carries enough light to read a surface
the figure is not merely a pair of lights in a void

detail.note: high here with B01 also failing is exactly the failure the founder named: eyes blazing, body gone. It is reported whether or not it passes, so the two can never be traded.

tests.name: the ground beside the character is readable too

detail.note: measured on the CONTROL frame, with the figure hidden, because the same band beside a figure reads 0.032 for one costume and 0.680 for another at one place and hour. The per-skin bands and the spill are reported beside it rather than gating: a mascot that lights the ground it stands on is not a mascot floating in blackness, whatever its own body reads.

tests.name: the mascot's own shadow is deep but not a hole

detail.note: the fraction of the beside-ground's light that the figure's shadow removes. Under 0.15 is a mascot that does not appear to be standing on anything; over 0.85 is a black hole where its feet should be. Both are failures and one number cannot be raised to fix the other.

tests.name: every figure still has a shape at night, bright or dark

detail.note: form is the standard deviation across the whole figure: surfaces differing from one another is what makes a figure read as one. This is the clause a luminous skin must pass; whether it should be luminous at all is the founder's call, not this job's.

tests.name: night still looks like night: the body is clearly darker than it is at noon

detail.note: the guard against fixing this by turning night into day. Above 1.0 the figure is its own light source, which world lighting cannot cause and which is a founder question about the skin; between the ceiling and 1.0 the night is genuinely too bright. Only the second fails.

tests.name: no figure is more of a light source at night than it is in daylight

detail.derivation: eye glow dims 24 to 8 across the day-night crossover, a factor of three, while the world at the arrival dims about 1.36. So this ratio should fall by roughly two at night. A value above 1.0 means it rose instead, and the bound is the crossover's own arithmetic rather than a threshold chosen here.

stood_at.note: the reading below describes THIS place. A body that reads well within a lamp's radius has not shown that the world lights bodies.

framing.note: body cells are everything in the box under the light threshold; the ground band is the strip immediately below it

clean_instrument.why: zero glow geometry, so its body is lit entirely by the world, and it is the canonical mascot.
